done_when: forge story new <KEY> "<title>" works for a story that has no spec: the story's own branch adds it to the roadmap, the plan's Why carries the problem, and the story gets one read loop and one approval; stories made from a spec work as today and specs stay optional. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Functional. When a client has any active roadmap item, `_idle` returns at lines 345–349 before reaching the new problem-card path. It tells the agent to run `forge story new` only for an item already on the roadmap. A client with an existing backlog and a newly discovered problem therefore still receives the old roadmap prerequisite as its next step, despite the command now accepting a new key. The discovery test exercises only an empty roadmap.
findings.title: Forge next still directs clients with a populated roadmap to choose an existing item

why: A new story needs a spec, its own read loop, a confirmation and a roadmap fix before its plan can even start
